$schema-note: One theme preset (design brief 2026-08-27, §4.5). A preset is a complete designed look: two authored palettes, a type map for all four roles, shape and texture and density, a motif default, and the curated option sets from the visual story.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings — the generator writes the RGB triples (brief §3.6). The dark palette is authored value by value; no dark value is derived from its light twin. The palette stays quiet and earthy so the linework carries the character.
$tier-note: Stability tier (owner review, 2026-08-27). See design/tokens/presets/civic.json for what the two tiers mean.
label: Field Guide
summary: A naturalist's expedition handbook. Plates, specimen labels, and observation notes, with the linework carrying the character.
$palette-words-light: near-neutral plate stock with a trace of warmth, soft bark ink, deep leaf green, muted clay, lichen-grey rule, herbarium cream, pressed archive, pencil grey
$palette-words-dark: near-neutral night ground with a trace of warmth, bone-white text, lifted moss green, lifted clay, moth-grey rule, lantern warmth, nocturne slate, faded field-note grey
$ground-note: Owner review, 2026-08-27: the ground was too warm. A tan canvas paired with earthy ink reads as the look #109 rejected, and it fought every client logo that was not itself brown. Surface, alt surface, and both inks move most of the way to neutral. Warmth is kept as a trace — a few channels of red over blue, no more — so the story is still a paper handbook and not a spreadsheet. The leaf-green primary and the clay accent are untouched: they are the theme's colour, and the ground is what had to get out of their way.
$font-note: Brief §9.2. Field Guide points both value roles at IBM Plex Mono on purpose: a label in this world is a tag, and a tag is set in the exact hand.
$shape-note: Texture is flat by default (owner review, 2026-08-27). Brief §4.5 already called it "flat with an optional light paper tone"; the optional tone was on. Flat surfaces are the shared default everywhere, and the tone is one advanced setting away.
$motif-note: Motifs are off by default (owner review, 2026-08-27). Brief §3.8 turned `botanical` on for Field Guide. Drawings on every page of a client's real programme read as decoration, not as observation, so the set is now something a client enables when their subject supports it. `botanical` is still the theme's set, and it is one pick away in the Illustrations control.
$tokens-note: Preset-level remaps of existing tier 2 and tier 3 tokens. No new property name (brief §3.4). The plate frame is a hairline; the double rule is the plate device's own doubling. The specimen label is the one preset that turns its rules and its field names on: a label in this world is a tag, and a tag states what each field is.

headingFace.label: Heading face
headingFace.prompt: The plate caption. Body stays Vollkorn and data stays IBM Plex Mono under every option.

choices.label: Besley
choices.why: The printed plate caption. Its Clarendon weight holds a title page and still sits calmly under a drawing, which is the core Field Guide relationship.

choices.label: Vollkorn bold at display size
choices.why: The one-face volume: a pocket handbook rather than a plate book, quieter and closer to the reading, and it adds nothing to the font budget.

choices.label: Spectral semibold
choices.why: The collector's volume. Its finer, sharper serifs read as the frontispiece of a formal edition, so the story gains a more scholarly opening.

nameplate.label: Nameplate treatment
nameplate.$default-note: The ruled title is the default (owner review, 2026-08-27). Plate framing is reserved for content that supports it. An event name and a date range are not a botanical plate, so the frame moved to the alternate; the empty-state plate stays, because a blank sheet IS what that content is.

choices.label: Ruled title, no frame
choices.why: The title page of a cheaper printing of the same book; quieter, and better for text-heavy events.

choices.label: Framed title page
choices.why: Name and dates inside a hairline frame with the nameplate-mark motif above the name. The opening plate of the handbook.

choices.label: Plate and label
choices.why: It states the book's subject the way a frontispiece plate does, and the plate stays drawn linework, never a photo.

choices.label: Specimen label
choices.why: A small ruled block: name, date, place. The collection tag.

choices.label: Field notes column
choices.why: The observation notebook rather than the mounted collection; it suits a single-track event where the day reads as one sitting.

marginalia.label: Pencil line
marginalia.prompt: The one piece of marginalia this theme allows. Its own control, so a client can keep the plates clean.

choices.label: Off
choices.why: The plates stay clean. This is the default, because a field notebook is written by someone being careful.

choices.label: On
choices.why: A thin hand-drawn underline under a specimen label or a note line: a pencil mark in a notebook, never a highlighter.
